newsitem.title: USA: First Albany opens Chicago office; first in Midwest.
newsitem.headline: First Albany opens Chicago office; first in Midwest.

text.p: First Albany Corp. said Tuesday it opened an office in Chicago, its first in the Midwest.
First Albany, a full-service brokerage, asset management and investment banking firm, also said it hired three former executives from Oppenheimer & Co. to establish the new office.
A First Albany spokesman said the company plans to hire between 10 and 12 brokers to staff the office over the next 12 months.

The newest office will be headed by Michael Stoken, 56, who will hold the titles of senior vice president and resident manager. Eric Kuby, 37, and Peter Gottlieb, 30, will both serve as vice presidents and portfolio managers for First Albany Asset Management.

First Albany said Stoken served previously as senior vice president and sales manager for Oppenheimer. Kuby was a senior vice president and portfolio manager with Oppenheimer Investment Advisors and Gottlieb was vice president of Oppenheimer & Co., First Albany said.
